bell_score_baseline.title: How would you describe your typical day?
bell_score_baseline.subtitle: This is the Bell CFS Disability Scale, the scale most ME/CFS clinicians and patients use. Pick whichever description feels closest most days.
bell_score_baseline.100: 100 — No symptoms at rest, no symptoms with exercise, normal overall activity, able to work full-time
bell_score_baseline.90: 90 — No symptoms at rest, mild symptoms with activity, normal overall activity, able to work full-time
bell_score_baseline.80: 80 — Mild symptoms at rest, symptoms worsened by exertion, minimal activity restriction for exertion only
bell_score_baseline.70: 70 — Mild symptoms at rest, some daily activity limitation, functions close to 90% of expected
bell_score_baseline.60: 60 — Mild to moderate symptoms at rest, daily activity limitation, functions 70-90%, can't work full-time in physical jobs
bell_score_baseline.50: 50 — Moderate symptoms at rest, moderate to severe with exercise, overall activity level 70% of expected
bell_score_baseline.40: 40 — Moderate symptoms at rest, moderate to severe with exercise, overall activity level 50-70% of expected
bell_score_baseline.30: 30 — Moderate to severe symptoms at rest, severe with any exercise, overall activity reduced to 50% of expected
bell_score_baseline.20: 20 — Moderate to severe symptoms at rest, unable to do strenuous activity, overall activity 30-50% of expected
bell_score_baseline.10: 10 — Severe symptoms at rest, bedridden most of the time, no travel outside the house
bell_score_baseline.0: 0 — Severe symptoms continuously, bedridden constantly, unable to care for self

pem_onset_delay.title: When do symptoms usually hit after exertion?
pem_onset_delay.subtitle: PEM often doesn't show up right away. Knowing your pattern helps Mya link crashes back to what actually caused them.
